references.text: God's prophecy to Abraham that his descendants would be oppressed in a foreign land for four hundred years, fulfilled here with the Egyptians' oppression of the Israelites.
Moses sees the Israelites' forced labor and burdens, which is a direct continuation of the oppression described in this verse.
Pharaoh accuses Moses and Aaron of distracting the people from their forced labor (sivlotam), the same word used in 1:11.
God promises to free the Israelites from the Egyptians' burdens (sivlot), referring back to the forced labor imposed on them.
A confession that recalls the harsh treatment and oppression of the Israelites by the Egyptians.
Pithom and Ramses are mentioned as part of the areas where the Israelites lived, called Goshen.
A poetic reference to God's deliverance of Israel from the burden (sevel), recalling the forced labor in Egypt.
Stephen's speech describes how a new king oppressed the ancestors of the Israelites and forced them to expose their infants.
Moses chose to suffer with God's people rather than enjoy the fleeting pleasures of sin, a reference to the oppression in Egypt.
